Всероссийский научно-исследовательский в: All-Russian Research Veterinary Institute of Poultry Farming
история параграф 1: «The All-Russian Scientific Research Veterinary Institute of Poultry Farming» (VNIVIP) is the oldest veterinary forge for the spread of bird diseases in poultry farms.
история параграф 2: The Institute's history dates back to Tsarist Russia. On August 17, 1808, Alexander I issued a decree establishing the charter of the Medical-Surgical Academy, which established a veterinary department, thus establishing the first higher veterinary educational institution.
история параграф 3: The opening of the veterinary department at the St. Petersburg Medical-Surgical Academy played a crucial role in the development of veterinary science and the training of veterinary personnel in Russia.
история параграф 4: In 1846, the first veterinary society was founded in St. Petersburg, and the first issue of the journal «Notes on Veterinary Medicine and Cattle Breeding» was published. This journal was directed and edited by I.I. Ravich. Its role in the development of veterinary science and the implementation of its achievements was exceptionally significant.
история параграф 5: In 1898, at the initiative of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Russian Empire, the first veterinary bacteriology laboratory in Russia was established in St. Petersburg. Until World War I in 1914, it was the largest and most authoritative base for veterinary science. The laboratory not only conducted diagnostics but also prepared vaccines and trained veterinarians in bacteriology. In 1917, training courses for veterinarians were officially approved. Until 1914, it was the largest and most authoritative base for veterinary science.
история параграф 6: During the Civil War, part of the laboratory was moved to Kuzminki in Moscow. The rest, along with all the premises, remained in St. Petersburg. After the October Revolution, the All-Union Institute of Experimental Veterinary Medicine (VIEV) was established in Kuzminki on the premises of the relocated laboratory. The St. Petersburg Veterinary Bacteriology Laboratory was reorganized into the Veterinary Bacteriology Institute of the People's Commissariat of Health of the RSFSR, later renamed (in 1936) the Leningrad Veterinary Research Institute.
история параграф 7: In 1964, the Leningrad Veterinary Research Institute was reorganized into the All-Union Research Institute for Poultry Diseases, with branch research and production laboratories for poultry diseases in Pyatigorsk and Kalinin, and transferred to the Poultry Industry of the USSR Ministry of Agriculture. In 1975, it was renamed the All-Union Veterinary Research Institute for Poultry Farming, and in 1991, the All-Russian Veterinary Research Institute for Poultry Farming.
история параграф 8: The main objectives of the Institute were to conduct fundamental research in veterinary matters in poultry farming, train scientific personnel, improve the qualifications of poultry veterinarians, and coordinate scientific research on the issue of «Veterinary prevention in industrial poultry farming».
история параграф 9: Following its reorganization in 1964, the Institute began studying infectious conjunctivitis, pseudoplague, smallpox, and infectious laryngotracheitis in fowl; the causes of tuberculin allergy in chickens without tuberculosis; pullorazine; pasteurellosis; the etiology and diagnosis of fowl lymphomatosis; the role of bacteria, fungi, and viruses in avian embryonic pathology; and methods for combating coccidiosis, nematodes, and ectoparasites in chickens. These topics were developed primarily on state and collective poultry farms, as well as in the Institute's laboratories, which were equipped with modern equipment.
история параграф 10: The first director of the Institute was a prominent parasitologist and brilliant organizer of science, Doctor of Veterinary Sciences, Professor V.F. Gusev.
история цитата: Our mission is - to protect the health of birds and ensure food security for the country through advanced veterinary research and practices.
